transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. It’s especially bad when I’m supposed to sit quietly and deal with paperwork or go over household plans with someone. I get really restless, like I need to move or do something else, and it’s starting to get hard to manage.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks when you're feeling restless?

Yes, definitely. I’ll sit down to read a planning email or a chapter of a book, and at first I’m okay. But after a few minutes I realize I’m just staring at the same paragraph over and over, and none of it has actually gone in.
Do you feel anxious or upset when you're feeling restless?
I’m not sure I’d call it anxious exactly. I get frustrated when I can’t settle down, but I haven’t really noticed it as fear or panic or anything like that.
Do you often act on impulse when you're feeling restless?

Yes, I do. I really try to be respectful, but I’ll jump into my husband’s conversations or finish what someone is saying before they’re done. It’s like the answer is out of my mouth before I’ve made myself wait.
Do you often fidget or tap your hands or feet when you're sitting still?

Yes. If I’m sitting still for a while, like in church meetings or at family dinners, I’ll catch myself twisting my wedding ring or bouncing my foot. I also shift around in the chair a lot, even when I’m trying to look like I’m sitting calmly.
Do you feel restless and have trouble sitting still in all situations, or are there certain places or activities where you feel more able to calm down and focus?

It’s more certain situations. I feel it most when I’m supposed to sit quietly and focus, like doing paperwork or going over household plans with someone. That’s when I really feel like I can’t settle in my own body.
Do you feel upset or irritable when you can't settle down or focus?
I’m not really sure. I know I get frustrated when I can’t focus, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it turns into irritability. It’s more like I just feel stuck and uncomfortable.
Did you experience restlessness or difficulty sitting still when you were a child?

Yes, looking back, I think it was already there in elementary school. I was the kid with the messy desk and forgotten permission slips, and I remember teachers sending notes home that I talked out of turn or couldn’t seem to stay in my seat.
Do you often forget things like appointments, deadlines, or tasks you need to complete?

Yes, that happens a lot. I’ll mean to return a call, pay a bill, or bring something with me to a meeting, and then suddenly days have gone by—or I’m already in the car before I remember. It’s frustrating because I really do intend to do it.
Do you have difficulty organizing tasks and activities, aside from just having trouble sitting still or focusing?
I’m not sure. I guess I’d need to think about what you mean by organizing tasks. I know I can feel scattered sometimes, but I haven’t really separated that from just having trouble focusing.
Do you have trouble waiting for your turn in lines or when doing group activities?

Yes, I do. Waiting in line, like at the pharmacy, makes me really tense and fidgety. And in meetings, if I have to wait until it’s my turn to speak, I notice I’m kind of sitting there checking the time over and over, just feeling impatient.
Have your restlessness and difficulty focusing affected your relationships with family or friends?

Yes. It’s caused problems. People at home and in the volunteer groups I’m part of can’t always count on me to follow through, even when I really mean to. I’ve had to step back from some responsibilities because I kept letting things fall through, and that feels pretty embarrassing.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they've finished speaking?

Yes, I do. I try really hard to be respectful, but sometimes I jump into my husband’s conversations or finish what someone is saying because the response is already coming out before I make myself wait. It’s not that I mean to cut people off, but it happens.
Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness and difficulty focusing consistently throughout your adult life?
I’ve had some of it for a long time, but it’s been noticeably worse since I got married and our routines merged. That was about a year and five months ago. Since then it’s just been harder to ignore.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt completely free of both restlessness and difficulty focusing?

No, I don’t think so. Looking back, it was already there when I was in elementary school. I was the girl with the messy desk, forgetting permission slips, and getting notes from teachers that I talked out of turn or couldn’t seem to stay seated. So I can’t really remember a time when both of those things were just gone.
Have your symptoms of restlessness and difficulty focusing been present for more than 6 months?
Yes. It’s definitely been more than 6 months. It’s been noticeably worse since I got married and our routines merged, which was about a year and five months ago.
Have your symptoms of restlessness and difficulty focusing caused you significant distress or problems in your daily life or relationships?

Yes, it has. It’s caused problems at home and with people I volunteer with. People can’t always count on me to follow through, even when I really mean to. I’ve had to step back from some responsibilities because things kept slipping through the cracks, and that’s been upsetting.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any other mental health conditions?
No, not that I know of. I haven’t had another mental health diagnosis.
Do you have any close relatives, such as parents or siblings, who have been diagnosed with ADHD?
I’m not sure. No one in my immediate family has told me they’ve been diagnosed with it, at least not that I know of.
Do you have trouble focusing or making mistakes in multiple areas of your life, such as at work, at home, or in social situations?

Yes. It happens in different places. Like, I’ll make a volunteer sign-up sheet or work on our household budget, and later I’ll notice I put in the wrong date, skipped a line, or reversed some numbers. And I really thought I had checked it, so it’s frustrating.
